value.body: An instrumentation engineer selects, installs, calibrates and maintains the instruments that measure pressure, flow, level and temperature in plants, and the control loops built on them. Employers include refineries, chemical and fertiliser plants, power stations, steel and pharma plants, and engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) firms. A typical day involves loop checks, reviewing instrument datasheets and drawings, and fixing faulty instruments with the operations team.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Transmitters, control valves, DCS/PLC, P&IDs, loop drawings

items.label: Work setting
items.value: Operating plants, project sites and design offices

items.label: GATE Instrumentation Engineering (IN) paper
items.source: GATE 2025 Statistical and Performance Report, IIT Roorkee

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as graduate engineer trainees in process plants, as trainee engineers at EPC or design firms (instrument datasheets, specifications and hook-up drawings), or with instrument makers and service companies. A plant internship and familiarity with P&IDs help.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Control valves and process control loops

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift and site work are common in operating plants.
Design roles at EPC firms are office-based and documentation-heavy.
Next roles: senior instrument engineer, C&I lead, project or maintenance manager.
